title: Project Mosaic: Layered Cost Controls (adaptive batching, KV prefetch, quant profiles)
creator: Lucia Chen
description: Goal: Deliver an incremental, low-risk initiative that reduces per-token serving costs 8–15% for mid-tail traffic by combining adaptive batching, selective KV prefetching, and conservative quantization profiles. Scope: (1) Instrument request classification to pick conservative batching and quant profiles per route; (2) Implement a lightweight KV prefetch heuristic for repeat prefixes; (3) Expose per-route knobs and rollout flags in Console for controlled experiments. Success metrics: 8–15% cost reduction on target routes, <5% latency regressions at p50 and <10% at p95, no customer-facing quality regressions as measured by existing eval suites.
acceptance_criteria: 1) End-to-end implementation gated behind a feature flag and Console controls; 2) Automated canary with traffic split proving cost savings on internal shadow routes; 3) Regression alerts integrated into Optimize and Console; 4) Playbook page for SRE/SE with rollback steps and observability queries.
deliverables: console: per-route controls and rollout UI
eval: prompt set coverage and automated checks
updates: 2026-02-22 - Lucia Chen: Draft PRD posted; initial trade-offs called out between batching granularity and p95 latency. Linked runtime owners for feasibility.
2026-02-28 - Marco Alvarez: Scoped MVP to two high-volume public routes and one internal shadow route. Estimate refined to 8 points. Added ENG-54122 and ENG-54890 as dependencies.

2026-03-05 - Priya Singh (Eng): Prototype adaptive batching policy with simulated traffic — shows 11% token-cost reduction in offline replay, added conservative caps to avoid batch growth for tail requests.
2026-03-10 - Marco Alvarez: Kickoff with SRE and Runtime teams; canary plan approved. Console product mockups delivered; linking to Console PM for UX review.
comments: Jamal Rivera (Lead Research): Concern about quant profile drift on instruction-heavy prompts; recommends a small eval set to catch delta in semantic quality.
Asha Nair (SRE): Request explicit observability for batch sizes and batch wait-time per route; added standard query set for incident debugging.
Priya Singh (Runtime Eng): Need a design decision for where prefetch logic lives (gateway vs serving runtime); prefer runtime for cache locality but cost of rollout is higher.
Marco Alvarez: Agreed to a two-phase approach: runtime pilot for internal shadow routes; gateway experiment for initial low-risk customer routes.
Design Review: Console UX needs clear risk indicators and a revert button on rollout page.
